Subject: Post-demo: SLO details & dedicated sizing next steps

Alex — thanks again for your time on the demo earlier. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned for sizing the dedicated pool and validating SLOs.

Recap (what I heard)
- Target p95 generation latency: <= 180 ms for streaming responses (typical reply length ~250 tokens).
- Concurrency: need to sustain ~120 concurrent streaming sessions at peak.
- Expected peak sustained RPS: ~220 requests/sec during business-hour bursts; average session token emission ~8 tokens/sec.
- Quality: full FP16 or int8 quantized models acceptable so long as token-level quality stays within your eval thresholds.

Sizing ask for Novus pilot
- We need your historic token distribution and a short trace (attached) so we can map to reserved throughput needs.
- Proposed pilot: 2-week performance pilot with a reserved pool configured to the SLO above and a parallel cost-optimized run to compare GPU types (H100 vs A100 vs L4).

Immediate next steps
1) Alex — please confirm the p95 target above and attach the token distribution/trace. (I attached our calibration sheet and a blank SLO calculator.)
2) Once we have traces we’ll size a reserved throughput target and send a recommended pilot config (GPU types, instance counts, bench plan).
3) Ben/Dylan/Karthik — I’m looping you for a technical sizing + pilot runbook draft; please flag anything we should lock before provisioning.

Attachments: novus_token_distribution.csv (requested), redwood_slo-calcs.xlsx (our worksheet)

Thanks —

Lauren — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the numbers and attaching the artifacts you asked for.

Confirmations and clarifications:
- p95 target: 180 ms is correct for streamed tokens (we observe p50 ~ 75ms today with our lighter model).
- Average reply footprint: 250 tokens per response (generation only).
- Peak traffic: roughly 220 rps sustained for 30–45 minute bursts; daily peak concurrent sessions ~120 as you noted.
- Important: ~40% of sessions are streaming (we send incremental tokens to the client), 60% are short-sync requests.

I attached: novus_token_distribution.csv (token histogram), novus_trace_sample.json (10-min sampled trace). The traces include a mix of short-sync and streaming sessions.

Two asks from our side before pilot provisioning:
1) Can you include a streaming-oriented benchmarking plan (how you’ll measure p95 across the stream vs end-to-end reply time)?
2) We'd like a cost-band estimate for each GPU option you’ll propose for the pilot (rough monthly committed cost and projected per-token cost delta).

Subject: RE: Post-demo: SLO details & dedicated sizing next steps (tech notes)

Team — reviewed Novus traces and token distribution. High-level sizing notes and GPU tradeoffs for the pilot below. Math is intentionally conservative to allow for KV cache/IO overhead.

Observed signals from trace
- Mean tokens per response: 250; mean token emission rate during streaming segments: ~8 tokens/sec.
- Peak concurrent streaming sessions: 120 → effective token emit load ~960 tokens/sec from streams. Add short-sync spikes (220 rps with avg 250 tokens = bursty additional ~55k tokens over a minute). For steady reserve we should size to ~2,500 tokens/sec to cover sustained streaming + short spikes with headroom.

GPU throughput roughs (in our current runtime with quantized weights, using continuous batching):
- NVIDIA H100 80GB (SXM): single instance practical sustained throughput ~4,200 tokens/sec for the target model & 512-context streaming workload; p95 latency headroom for 120 concurrent streams.
- NVIDIA A100 80GB: sustained ~2,000 tokens/sec per instance under same quantized path; p95 meets target at lower concurrency but needs multiple instances for redundancy.
- NVIDIA L4 48GB (cost-optimized): ~420 tokens/sec per instance (int8 microkernel path) — cheaper per-node but requires 5–7x instances and has higher p95 variability on streaming workloads.

Instance counts to hit ~2,500 tokens/sec reserved throughput (baseline):
- H100: 1 instance (2,500 < 4,200; recommend 1 H100 with an extra standby for failover).
- A100: 2 instances (2 x 2,000 = 4,000; use 2 with autoscaling guard).
- L4: 6 instances (6 x 420 = 2,520; recommend 6 across two AZs for headroom + lower latency variance).

Qualitative tradeoffs
- H100: best single-node latency and cleanest streaming p95. Higher hourly cost but simpler operational surface for the pilot.
- A100: good middle ground; slightly higher infra count but lower cost than H100 for multi-instance configs.
- L4: best unit cost; more complex orchestration for KV caches and higher cross-node variance for streaming p95.

Quantization notes
- INT8 calibration yields ~1.1–1.3x throughput improvement with negligible quality hit on your eval slices. INT4 gives additional speed but requires careful eval gating — not recommended for initial pilot.

Recommendation (pilot plan)
1) Run a 2-week pilot using: Week A — 1 H100 reserved pool to validate streaming p95 on single-node; Week B — 2 A100s as cost-comparison mode.
2) Reserve throughput config: 2,500 tokens/sec baseline; expose per-token tracing & p95 dashboards.
3) Acceptance criteria: p95 <= 180ms for streamed tokens across 95% of sampled sessions and error rate < 0.5%.

I'll draft a bench plan (step-by-step: load profiles, token gating, KV cache priming) and a short runbook for provisioning.

Karthik
